builder.objective: REPAIR V3-06: Wire the same materialization + dirty-record recording into the SQLite path (e.g. SqliteSyncStateRepository.applyDeltas materializes into Sqlite business tables, and Sqlite business repos record dirty sync records after writes), covering all 8 SYNC_COLLECTIONS including persistent_tasks, members, memberships and households. Add a test that exercises the SQLite repository path (or a shared contract test run against both implementations) proving remote delta -> business record readable + local write -> getDirtyRecords payload.; Wrap cursor advance + materialization in a single transaction (extend in-memory withTransaction snapshot coverage to all affected repos, and use withTransactionAsync on SQLite): materialize first, then advance the cursor, atomically; on failure roll back both so the delta is re-fetched on the next pull.; Enforce membership scoping in the data-access path: repository or use-case layer must verify the caller's membership for every read/write (e.g. a scoped repository facade taking the caller userId and checking memberships before getByHousehold/create/update/delete), and ledger mutations must go through append/revision/tombstone with assertLedgerWrite-style validation. Hostile tests must prove a non-member read/write is rejected through the actual repository path.; Track and persist the local revision of each synchronized entity (revision column on business tables or sync metadata), pass the real local revision to resolveConflict in the materializer, apply resolveConflict to households (and members/memberships) as well, and make the SQLite applyDeltas use the same deterministic revision/timestamp/id resolution instead of blind overwrite. Add a materializer-level test where the local revision is higher than the remote and assert the local version wins.
builder.scope: Repair only the audited must-fix findings on the preserved V3 baseline; do not rebuild accepted work.

hostile tests: cross-tenant read blocked, balance falsification rejected, concurrent same-id edits resolved deterministically
end-to-end sync tests: remote delta materializes into business data, local write appears in getDirtyRecords and is pushed
